name: TRAD - Step-Wise Thought Retrieval and Aligned Decision
venue: SIGIR 2024 (Proceedings of the 47th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval); preprint arXiv:2403.06221
authors_affiliation: Ruiwen Zhou, Yingxuan Yang, Muning Wen, Ying Wen, Yong Yu, Weinan Zhang (Shanghai Jiao Tong University); Wenhao Wang, Chunling Xi, Guoqiang Xu (China Pacific Insurance). Lead author Ruiwen Zhou (Shanghai Jiao Tong University).
task_domain: LLM-agent sequential decision-making: embodied/text-game household tasks (ALFWorld) and web navigation (Mind2Web), plus real-world robotic process automation (RPA) on enterprise insurance websites.
problem_setting: Tuning-free in-context learning (ICL) LLM agents for sequential decision-making. The setting assumes access to a large memory of near-optimal expert trajectories (collected by humans or expert policies). The agent is interactive (multi-step, environment in the loop), single-agent, and not fine-tuned. Supervision is available only as expert trajectories (no reward); ground-truth actions are available offline for the memory but NOT at inference time. The core problem is automatic, per-task, per-step selection and effective utilization of in-context demonstration examples, addressing the failure modes of trajectory-level retrieval (plausible examples, LLM context limit, irrelevant context noise).
what_is_retrieved: Step-level expert demonstrations (individual decision steps from expert trajectories), each pre-labeled with a pseudo-golden 'thought' (CoT reasoning) used as the retrieval key. A coarse trajectory-level retrieval (Synapse-style, keyed on task meta-data) is also used as a first stage to enable thought generation.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external memory of expert trajectories (a fixed offline corpus). The memory is enriched once offline with pseudo-golden thoughts but does not grow during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-K ranking objective: TRAD retrieves the top-K most thought-similar steps (K in {1..5}, default 3 on Mind2Web, 2 on ALFWorld) belonging to mutually different trajectories. It is not framed as completeness/minimal-set recovery nor as precision-driven variable-size recommendation.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (thought-based step retrieval). Reuse: yes (retrieved steps + temporal neighbors used as ICL exemplars). Revise: no (no case adaptation/revision of stored cases). Retain: no (no write-back of new experiences). Flags: [Retrieve, Reuse, ~Revise(no), ~Retain(no)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself as step-wise demonstration/in-context-example retrieval and retrieval-augmented decision-making; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner or describe itself as case-based reasoning.
retrieval_unit: thought-step (a single decision step represented by its pseudo-golden thought). Sub-trajectory context is added afterward via temporal expansion, but the retrieval unit itself is a single step's thought.
index_source: Static, offline-induced memory of expert trajectories. Pseudo-golden thoughts for every memory step are induced offline by an LLM (prompted with ground-truth actions and a small human-thought-annotated seed subset). No online/test-time induction of the store.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index over thought embeddings (cosine-similarity search). A coarse trajectory-level index keyed on task meta-data (Synapse-style) is also maintained for first-stage trajectory retrieval; retrieved steps are constrained to come from mutually different trajectories.
retriever_type: Dense retriever using off-the-shelf pretrained sentence/passage encoders (Sentence-BERT, DPR). For the first-stage trajectory retrieval, Synapse's task-meta-data similarity is reused.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The dense encoder is a frozen pretrained retriever (Sentence-BERT / DPR); it is not trained on similarity labels, LM feedback, downstream-task signals, or RL. Selection is fixed cosine-similarity top-K over thought embeddings.
query_construction: Thought-conditioned query: at each timestep the LLM is prompted (with first-stage trajectory-retrieved demonstrations as exemplars) to generate a CoT 'thought' abstracting the current state; this thought is encoded as the dense query. Keys are the precomputed pseudo-golden thoughts of memory steps.
query_granularity: Two-level retrieval: (1) trajectory-level retrieval with task meta-data (one-shot, used only to generate the thought), then (2) step/state-level retrieval where the per-step generated thought is the query.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative (per-step). Thought retrieval is performed at every decision timestep of the rollout.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered at every timestep (one thought-retrieval per decision step). No uncertainty/confidence/learned-router trigger.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage. Selection is plain cosine-similarity top-K with a constraint that retrieved steps belong to mutually different trajectories.
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose / context shaping rather than rerank or compression: each retrieved step is temporally expanded into a short sub-sequence (B previous + F subsequent steps), annotated with relative-order marks ([Step -1], [Step 0], [Step 1] ...), and the current episode is history-aligned to match demonstration format. The overall effect is noise reduction by keeping only step-relevant context instead of full trajectories.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill descriptions; demonstrations are expert decision steps). Thought Preparation does synthesize pseudo-golden thoughts as retrieval keys for each memory step, which is an index-side text-engineering step.
index_content_separation: Partial: lightweight thought embeddings serve as the retrievable index/key, while the heavier step content (observation, action, neighboring steps) is loaded on demand for the chosen top-K steps. Not framed as progressive disclosure but functions similarly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (static memory; no live tool index, RapidAPI/REST/MCP protocol, or CRUD sync).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved step demonstrations, after temporal expansion + relative-order marking, are inserted into the LLM prompt as in-context exemplars; the LLM then predicts the next action conditioned on the current (history-aligned) observation. Retrieval is not a training signal and not latent.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-then-act. At each timestep: generate thought -> step-wise thought retrieval -> aligned-decision context shaping -> LLM predicts next action. No tree search / MCTS; integration is a per-step retrieval-augmented action policy.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-CoT-step / per-decision-step: one thought generation and one thought retrieval per action step within the rollout.
adaptation_mechanism: Verbatim ICL exemplar usage with context augmentation (no case revision). Retrieved steps are used as demonstrations and complemented by their temporal neighbors and order marks; the retrieved cases themselves are not adapted/edited.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw expert step demonstrations (observation-action pairs) augmented with pseudo-golden thoughts, temporally-neighboring steps, and relative-order position marks; injected as structured text exemplars in the prompt.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration step (raw step), with a distilled CoT-thought abstraction used as its retrieval handle; expanded into a short raw sub-trajectory for decision. Not a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Two complementary mechanisms: (1) step-wise thought retrieval reduces irrelevant context by selecting only step-relevant demonstrations (vs full noisy trajectories), mitigating plausible examples and context-limit/forgetting; (2) Aligned Decision (temporal expansion + relative-order mark + history alignment) provides tolerance for imperfect thoughts by supplying neighboring-step context, so an inaccurate query thought is used for retrieval rather than direct prediction.
memory_type: Episodic expert-trajectory memory (static), enhanced offline with pseudo-golden thoughts to support both trajectory-level and step-level retrieval.
write_back: False. No new experiences/cases are written back to memory during inference; the thought-enhanced memory is built once offline and remains fixed.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test-time; it is frozen after offline thought induction.
write_back_trigger: Never (no write-back). Offline, thoughts are added to memory steps once via LLM labeling, but there is no runtime write event triggered by success/failure/reflection.
failure_experience_usage: None. The memory contains only near-optimal expert (success) trajectories; failed/negative experiences are neither stored nor retrieved.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only at construction time (thoughts appended to memory steps offline); no runtime mutation, dedup, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or pruning.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed similarity top-K over a frozen pretrained encoder, not a learned/RL-optimized policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: ALFWorld (134 out-of-distribution tasks, 6 task types: Put/Examine/Clean/Heat/Cool/PutTwo); Mind2Web (3 subsets: Cross-Task, Cross-Website, Cross-Domain); plus real-world deployment on 4 enterprise insurance websites (20 unseen tasks each) at a global business insurance company (China Pacific Insurance).
benchmark_family: embodied (ALFWorld) and web (Mind2Web); plus real-world RPA/web-navigation deployment.
baselines: ReAct (Fixed), ReAct (Random), ReAct (Relevant) [Mind2Web]; Synapse (trajectory-level retrieval with task meta-data); Synapse + ReAct combination (ALFWorld); Synapse w/o Retrieval; MindAct (Mind2Web, no reasoning/retrieval). Real-world: ReAct-RD (random demo), ReAct-RV (relevant-trajectory demo), TR (TRAD w/o aligned decision).
key_metrics: ALFWorld: task Success Rate (SR). Mind2Web: Element Accuracy (Ele. Acc), Step Success Rate (Step SR), trajectory Success Rate (SR). Real-world deployment: Step SR and SR; plus inference time overhead (efficiency).
headline_result: On ALFWorld, TRAD reaches 96.77% average SR, a +2.99% improvement over the strongest baseline Synapse+ReAct (93.78% -> 96.77%), with GPT-4 and 2 in-context examples. On Mind2Web (GPT-3.5-turbo, 3 examples) TRAD improves over Synapse by +2.1% Ele.Acc, +1.4% Step SR, +0.5% SR overall (All: 32.5/28.0/2.1). Real-world deployment raises average Step SR 90.2%->98.1% and SR 65.0%->92.5%.
ablations: Aligned Decision component ablation on Mind2Web (GPT-3.5-turbo): removing Temporal Expansion (TE) hurts most across all subsets (it is the basic structure); removing History Alignment (HA) and Relative Order Mark (ROM) hurts the harder Cross-Website/Cross-Domain subsets but slightly helps Cross-Task (in-distribution). Hyper-parameter studies: expansion steps B (backward) and F (forward) varied 0->4 one-sided — both improve over no expansion; forward expansion (F) helps more than backward (B); best at F=2, B=0; large B/F adds no further gain (far context is noisy). Number of retrieved demonstrations K in {1..5}: K has mild effect and TRAD's advantage over Synapse is stable for K in {1..4} (Synapse exceeds context limit at K=5). Real-world TR vs TRAD ablation confirms both thought retrieval and aligned decision contribute.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (SR / Step SR / Ele. Acc) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both outcome and intermediate process: trajectory Success Rate (outcome) plus step-level process quality via Step SR and Element Accuracy (Mind2Web), which capture per-step decision correctness.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported efficiency: at inference TRAD adds only ~11.7% more time than ReAct-RD (the extra thought-retrieval step). Step-wise retrieval substantially reduces input context vs full-trajectory prompting, alleviating context-limit failures (Synapse exceeds the LLM context limit at K=5 while TRAD does not). Authors note ALFWorld/Mind2Web baseline choices were constrained by API cost limits.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-K selection with context-shaping: top-K steps (K=3 default on Mind2Web, K=2 on ALFWorld), each expanded to at most B+1+F steps (best F=2,B=0). Step-wise retrieval is explicitly motivated by staying within the LLM context budget where trajectory-level prompting overflows it.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a new benchmark; uses ALFWorld 134 OOD tasks and Mind2Web 3 subsets). The real-world deployment dataset (100 expert trajectories per website over 4 websites for memory; 20 unseen eval tasks per website) is author-collected but proprietary.
builds_on: Synapse (Zheng et al., 2024b — trajectory-level retrieval with task meta-data, ICL exemplars); ReAct (Yao et al., 2023b — reason-then-act CoT for agents); Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., 2022); dense retrievers Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych, 2019) and DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020); IRCoT (Trivedi et al., 2023 — closest prior, retrieval with reasoning steps for QA).
contrasts_with: Synapse (trajectory-wise retrieval/prompting — criticized for plausible examples, context-limit overflow, and irrelevant-context noise); IRCoT (retrieves with full historical trajectory and accumulates documents over time for QA, uses thoughts only as queries with raw docs as keys — TRAD instead retrieves distinct single steps across timesteps, uses single-step thoughts as both query and key, and adds temporal alignment for sequential decision-making); ReAct (Fixed/Random) which use non-retrieved or randomly retrieved demonstrations.
lineage: Group C (RAG planning): retrieval-augmented in-context demonstration selection for LLM-agent sequential decision-making. Advances the lineage from trajectory-level retrieval (Synapse) toward step-level / thought-aligned retrieval, and is the first to bring thought-based retrieval to sequential decision-making (extending IRCoT's QA-only reasoning-retrieval).
